title: AI System Card
description: One card per AI system in use. Maintained by the organisation from provider documentation — never generated by the model it describes. Answers: what is this, who runs it, where does our data go, and who is accountable.

system_name.description: How your organisation refers to this system.

eu_representative.description: AI Act Art. 22 authorised representative, where the provider is established outside the Union.

purpose.description: What your organisation uses it for. Specific enough to be a GDPR Art. 30 purpose.

role.description: Your role under the AI Act for this system. Rebranding a third-party system as your own, or substantially modifying it, can make you a provider.

annex_iii_category.description: Which Annex III point applies, if high-risk and standalone.

rationale.description: Why this classification. The reasoning matters more than the label.

data_flows.description: Where the data goes. The core of this card and the field most organisations cannot answer. One entry per recipient.

special_categories.description: Whether GDPR Art. 9 special-category data can reach this processor.

retention.description: Quote the provider's stated period, e.g. '30 days for abuse monitoring'.

used_for_training.description: Whether the processor trains on your data. 'unknown' is a valid and honest answer that should become an action item.

transfer_mechanism.description: SCCs, adequacy decision, derogation, or 'not applicable — EU processing'.

subprocessors.description: URL of the processor's subprocessor list.

dpa_reference.description: Where your DPA with this processor lives.

source.description: URL of the provider documentation these facts come from. Required in practice — see conventions in the README of protocol/examples.

article_50_disclosure.description: The transparency text actually shown to people, and where. Applies from 2 August 2026.

disclosure_text.description: Verbatim wording shown to the person.

where_shown.description: At which point in the interaction. Must be at the latest at first interaction or exposure — Art. 50(5).

marking_method.description: For Art. 50(2): the machine-readable marking technique used.

accessibility_notes.description: How the disclosure meets accessibility requirements — Art. 50(5).

exemption_claimed.description: If relying on an exemption, which one and why. E.g. 'Art. 50(4) editorial review — every published item is reviewed by a named editor, recorded in the AIDR.'

model.description: in_the_loop: a human approves each output. on_the_loop: a human monitors and can intervene. in_command: a human decides whether the system runs at all.

aidr_required.description: Whether this system must emit AI Decision Records.

legal_basis.description: GDPR basis for the personal data processed through this system.

special_category_basis.description: Art. 9(2) basis, where special-category data is involved.

dpia_reference.description: Where the DPIA lives — Art. 35, and AI Act Art. 26(9).

oversight_owner.description: The accountable human. A role alone is not enough — someone has to be reachable.

known_limitations.description: What this system is bad at. Honest entries here prevent misuse better than any policy.

incidents_reference.description: Path to the incident log for this system.

review_cycle.description: How often this card is re-verified, e.g. 'quarterly'.

last_verified.description: When a human last checked these facts against provider documentation. Provider terms change faster than laws — a card older than a quarter should be treated as unverified.

sources.description: URLs of the provider documentation this card is built from.
